text:
ryan: seeing a cluster-wide nvme stalls in us-central2 coincident with a spice-heavy model rollout. Attach-provisioner shows attach_wait 95p spikes and scheduler is queueing launches.

ops-bot: [alert] region=us-central2 metric=attach_wait severity=high value=11s baseline=1.2s

anya: any recent janitor/kernel changes in that region?

ryan: we rolled a runtime patch that changed writeback batching ~1h ago. Noticed more scrub churn in nvme logs.

vik: if writeback batching increased synchronous flushes, that can amplify write amplification and push drives into firmware writeback stalls. We should reduce writeback aggressiveness and start a targeted hot-slab reclaim.

storage-bot: [metric] us-central2 nvme_iops=15200 queue_depth=22 hot_pool_free_mb=780

maddie-support: customer reports for Dedicated attach timeouts are coming in. Sending status update to affected tenants.

anya: short-term: roll config: `rvctl svc config set runtime --region us-central2 --writeback-batch=small --apply-immediately` and throttle janitor concurrency. Also lower scheduler max-attach to 120 for region.

ryan: applying now. Running `janitor reclaim --region us-central2 --mode=selective --limit=100 --sleep-ms=300` to avoid IO bursts.

ops-bot: [info] config-change applied by anya for runtime/us-central2

(10m later)

storage-bot: [metric] us-central2 nvme_iops=8400 queue_depth=11 hot_pool_free_mb=2200 attach_wait95p=2.1s

vik: looks better. Plan items: 1) revert or canary the runtime writeback param in future; 2) add preflight iops surge prediction for writeback changes; 3) add device-thermal and firmware-stall detection to scheduler so it can avoid late binds to hot drives.

maddie-support: customers notified: "We've applied mitigations in us-central2 to reduce storage reclaim pressure; attach latency is improving. We'll keep monitoring for 1h."

ryan: cost note: we could replace ~12 degraded hosts to immediately reduce pressure, cost est ~+$1.8k; keeping this as option if queues don't settle. Filing a follow-up ticket and adding runbook steps + exact `rvctl` commands used.

anya: closing for now, will watch for regressions. If any follow-up needed I'll reopen. :thumbsup:
